transcript: Habari team, this is Grace Wanjiru, the CHV from Rongai. I want to report on today's family planning outreach at Kampi ya Moto dispensary. We started at nine in the morning with a short talk on the different methods, then the nurse, Sister Mary Chebet, gave services. In total, forty-two women came, and most of them were young mothers. Six women were referred to Rongai Health Centre for implants because we ran out of stock. One mama asked to be called for follow-up, her number is 0711 000 482. I will send the register tomorrow. Thank you.

Good evening everyone, it's Faith Achieng. I was also at the Kampi ya Moto outreach today with Grace. Just to confirm the numbers, we served forty-two women on family planning, and six were referred for implants. The turnout was very good, even though the rain started around noon. The women asked if we can come back next month, so maybe we can plan that. If anyone needs the photos, call me on 0722 000 917 and I will share them on WhatsApp. Asante.

Hello ladies, it's Rose Njeri here. Sorry I missed the meeting this morning, the matatu from Solai broke down on the way and we waited for almost two hours. Eeh, it was really bad. Anyway, I hope everyone is fine. Please remind me, who is bringing the tea and mandazi for Saturday? I can bring sugar. Also, if someone has a charger for a Tecno phone, I left mine at home. You can reach me on 0733 000 156. Okay, see you soon, bye bye.

Hi team, Beatrice Atieno here, reporting from the Tumaini women's group meeting in Mogotio. Today was our monthly table banking day. Twenty-five members attended out of thirty. Together they saved eighteen thousand shillings, and we gave out four small loans to members who are starting businesses, mostly selling vegetables and second-hand clothes. The treasurer, Mama Lucy Kiprop, recorded everything in the book. Our next meeting is on the fifteenth. If you need the records, Lucy's number is 0745 000 638.

Morning everyone, this is Janet Mwangi. Yesterday we went to Sarambei Primary School for the menstrual hygiene session with the girls in class six to eight. Sixty girls attended. We talked about periods, how to use and dispose of pads safely, and why they should not miss school. At the end, every girl received a pack of reusable sanitary pads. The head teacher, Mrs. Esther Koech, has asked us to come back and also talk to the mothers. Her phone number is 0790 000 274 if someone wants to follow up.

Hello team, it's Mercy Wambui. I want to share about the community dialogue on gender-based violence we held this afternoon at the chief's camp in Solai. Thirty-five women attended, plus a few village elders. The police gender desk officer, Corporal Ann Mutua, explained how to report cases and where survivors can get help. Some women shared their stories, it was very emotional. Three women asked for private follow-up, and we connected them with the counsellor. For anything about this session, you can call me on 0701 000 593.

Hi everyone, Sister Nancy Cherono here. Today we did the cervical cancer screening camp at Rongai Health Centre. We screened twenty-eight women. Most results were normal, but three women had positive results, so we referred them to Nakuru Level Five Hospital for further treatment. One of them is Mrs. Agnes Wairimu, and she has agreed to go on Monday. Please, whoever is going to Nakuru that day, help her with transport. Her number is 0768 000 341. I will upload the full report later.

Eeh, congratulations to Mama Purity Jeptoo on the new baby! We are so happy for you. Ladies, let's plan to visit her this weekend at her home in Kabarak, after church. I suggest we each contribute two hundred shillings for a small gift, maybe a baby blanket and some unga. Send your contribution to Ruth on M-Pesa, her number is 0756 000 819. And please, don't forget to bring your own chairs, last time we were standing. Okay, have a blessed evening.

Hello team, this is Caroline Nyambura reporting from Kampi ya Moto. Today we held the kitchen garden training for women farmers. Eighteen women attended. The agriculture officer, Mr. Peter Langat, showed them how to make a sack garden and how to make compost from kitchen waste. Each woman received seedlings of sukuma wiki and spinach to plant at home. Next month we will visit their homes to see how the gardens are doing. If you want to join the follow-up visits, call me on 0712 000 765.

Good evening, this is Joyce Muthoni. I was helping Sister Nancy at the screening camp in Rongai today. Just adding to her report: we had twenty-eight women screened for cervical cancer, and three were referred to Nakuru Level Five. The women were very happy because many of them had never been screened before. Next time we should bring more chairs and water because the queue was long. My number is 0729 000 408 if you need anything from me.
